title: daemon
description: The `daemon` content kind (megaplan 1.7 and tasks 6-A1, 6-B1, 6-S1): one Breach Protocol daemon. `sequence` is the fixed run of hex codes (2 to 4, from the six codes of the grid) the player must put into the buffer in that order; `kinds` lists the device kinds (section 1.11) whose breach may offer it; `action` is the real thing it does, one of the closed list the scripts implement (a datapack may re-skin an action with another name, sequence and strengths, but cannot invent an action); `tiers` holds exactly three rows, strength 1, 2 and 3 in that order (the server picks the strength from how many and how long the solved daemons are, section 6-B1): `seconds` is how long the effect lasts (for a one-shot action, how long its aftermath lasts) and `radius` the reach in blocks around the breached device (the scripts convert to Cyberpunk metres 1:1). `weight` is the relative chance the generator picks it among the daemons that fit; `min_security` is the lowest `breach_tier` security level (1 ordinary, 2 secure, 3 hardened) at which it is offered. `title_key` and `text_key` are lang keys (the name and one line of what it does). The daemon's wire id (the `daemon` message `list`) is the file name, for example `cyberblock:open_door`. Actions: open_door (doors and gates in reach unlock and open), disable_cameras (cameras in reach go dark), reveal_enemies (people in reach are outlined for the team), overload (the breached device and its neighbours short out and stun people near them), disable_turrets (turrets in reach stand down), lights_out (lights in reach switch off), distract (screens, vending machines and speakers draw people's attention), traffic_switch (traffic lights in reach change), make_friendly (turrets and cameras in reach turn friendly).
